subject: storytime
title: Henny Penny
about: The old English folk tale, also told as Chicken Little, about the hen who is bonked by an acorn, decides the sky is falling and sets off to tell the king with a line of friends behind her. The rhyming names and repeated lines make it a favorite for reading aloud, and it is a gentle way to talk about checking a scary story before you believe it. In this softened telling a wise owl stops everyone at the fox's den and shows them the acorn; it is a public-domain story retold in first-grade words, five pages long.
tip: Ask: what should Henny Penny have done before she ran off to tell the king?

book.author: a folk tale from England (retold)
book.source: public domain, retold in first-grade words
book.blurb: One acorn, one worried hen, and a long line of friends.

passage.text:
One day Henny Penny was pecking in the yard.
Plop!
An acorn fell on her head.
"Oh, my!" said Henny Penny.
She was scared.
"The sky is falling!"
"I must go and tell the king."
On the way she met Cocky Locky.
"The sky is falling!" said Henny Penny.
"I am going to tell the king."
"I will come, too," said Cocky Locky.
***
Soon they met Ducky Lucky.
"The sky is falling!" said Henny Penny.
"We are going to tell the king."
"I will come, too," said Ducky Lucky.
Then they met Turkey Lurkey.
"Where are you going?" he asked.
"The sky is falling!" said Henny Penny.
"We are going to tell the king."
"I will come, too," said Turkey Lurkey.
Off they all went.
***
Then they met Foxy Loxy.
"Where are you going?" he asked.
"The sky is falling!" said Henny Penny.
"We are going to tell the king."
Foxy Loxy smiled a sly smile.
"I know a short way," he said.
"Come into my den."
"Oh, thank you," said Henny Penny.
And they all walked toward the den.
***
"Stop!" called a voice from a tree.
It was a wise old owl.
"Stay out of that den!"
"Henny Penny, did you look up?" asked the owl.
"No," said Henny Penny.
The owl held up a little brown acorn.
"This is an acorn," he said.
"Acorns fall from oak trees."
"One fell on your head."
"The sky is just fine."
***
Henny Penny looked up.
The sky was blue and still.
"It was only an acorn," she said.
Foxy Loxy gave a huff and ran off.
"Thank you, Owl," said Henny Penny.
Then they all went home for supper.
Henny Penny, Cocky Locky, Ducky Lucky, and Turkey Lurkey.
Nobody told the king.
Check before you believe a scary story.

cards.q: What fell on Henny Penny's head?
cards.note: Plop, one little brown acorn from the oak tree, and she never looked up to check.

cards.q: Who did Henny Penny want to tell?
cards.note: She was sure the sky was falling and that the king had to know.

cards.q: Where did Foxy Loxy want them to go?
cards.note: He smiled a sly smile and said it was a short way to the king.

cards.q: Who stopped them at the fox's den?
cards.note: The owl called stop from a tree and showed everyone what had really fallen.

cards.q: What happened first in the story?
cards.note: The whole story starts with one plop on Henny Penny's head.

cards.q: What happened at the end of the story?
cards.note: Nobody told the king, and they all went home for supper instead.

cards.q: How did Henny Penny feel when the acorn hit her head?
cards.note: She was so scared she did not stop to look at what had hit her.
Check before you believe a scary story; the last line says it.

cards.q: In the story, what does 'sly' mean?
cards.note: A sly fox is a tricky one, and his short way to the king was really a trick.

cards.q: Which word is in the story?
cards.note: He reads the three words himself; only one of them is in the story.
